title: A critical-point criterion for D-stability in every dimension
abstract: Johnson's contact criterion for D-stability is expressed as an explicit principal-minor critical-point system. For every real square matrix and every choice of positive barrier weights, D-stability is equivalent to Hurwitz stability and the absence of positive solutions of the associated Fritz-John equations. The proof applies a proper exhaustion of the positive orthant to Johnson's contact variety, so that every nonempty contact set contains a critical point. In dimension five, the criterion is written explicitly as a Lagrange system and a tangency system, with coefficients given by principal minors. Both equivalences are formalized in Lean. The result applies the classical critical-point method to the characterization problem discussed by Kanovei and Logofet (1998) and Kushel (arXiv:2604.16526).
